correctness.rationale: For each fixed n, the derivative substitution reduces b_n² to n/π times the minimal monic degree-(n−1) planar L² norm. The exact Taylor-jet disk identity is π∑ r^(2j+2)|q^(j)(±a)/j!|²/(j+1). Symmetry and uniqueness force odd/even minimizers. The injective k-jet map on each parity subspace bounds coefficients and proves convergence to z(z²−a²)^(k−1) for degree 2k−1 and (z²−a²)^k for degree 2k. Their first nonzero jets give b_(2k)~(2ar)^k and b_(2k+1)~2^k a^k r^(k+1) sqrt[2(2k+1)/(k+1)]. Circle equilibrium-energy bounds sqrt(2ar) <= cap(K) <= sqrt(2r(a+r)), proving capacity equivalence. No uniform-in-degree conclusion. Independently solved exact rational Gram matrices n=1..8 at radii 1/30 and 1/120, 16 cases consistent with asymptotic constants (within 3%).
